title: Passwords in one minute
subtitle: Two rules, two accounts, one of them comes back

cards.title: Two rules, and then you do it
cards.say: We have a minute, so here is the short version. A guesser's machine does not care about your exclamation mark. It cares how much there is to get through, and whether it has seen your password somewhere else already.

rules.headline: Long beats clever.
rules.body: Four unrelated words. A short password with symbols in it is still short.

rules.headline: Never the same one twice.
rules.body: One leaked site becomes every site, because attackers replay the pairs they already have.

cards.sign_off: The full lesson adds two more rules and five password managers to pick from. This is the minute version.

sections.question: How are you feeling about this?

levels.label: Still unsure
levels.reply: Quite all right, dear. Two accounts, and nothing you type here unlocks anything anywhere.

levels.label: Getting there
levels.reply: Good. Prove it on two accounts, and save both as you go.

levels.label: Confident
levels.reply: Confident? Two should be no trouble then. I will be waiting at the end to say which one I would have tried first.

cards.title: Now the part that proves it
cards.say: Two pretend sites, one of them holding a card number. Invent a new password for each. We keep a scrambled fingerprint so you can log back in, and nothing else: not the password, not a hint, not a way to remind you.

rules.headline: Two sites, two new passwords.
rules.body: Both pretend, both ours, and they unlock nothing. Do not use a password you really have, not even once.

rules.headline: We will ask for one of them back.
rules.body: In a moment, one of the two at random. We will not say which, so the only way through is to have saved both.

cards.sign_off: Two accounts. Then we find out whether the habit is real.
